subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps by adding TUI-owned viewport/follow policy, by patching or upgrading pi-tui rendering, or by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll setting?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix crosses terminal UX policy, dependency behavior, and possible settings surface rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose terminal user control if maintainers want explicit preference behavior, accepting the extra settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Keep this open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest recent routing candidate for adjacent TUI state and lifecycle changes in the current history.
